## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10) is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and concluding text of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka in the Pali Canon. In the architecture of the Theravāda Abhidhamma, the *mahantaraduka* constitutes the "longer intermediate set of fourteen dyads" within the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*), addressing miscellaneous pairs of conditional factors, many of which specifically analyze the mutual relations between awareness (*citta*) and mental states (*cetasika*) [Potter 1996]. Within the *Paṭṭhāna*, this section subjects these fourteen dyads to the comprehensive system of twenty-four conditional relations (*paccaya*).

Direct secondary scholarship on this specific *Paṭṭhāna* chapter is minimal, as modern scholarship on the *mahantaraduka* dyads primarily discusses their enumeration in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi*, their treatment in the *Dhātukathā*, and their broader structural position within the Abhidhamma *mātikā*.
